data.narrative:
DIRAC is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Fil Aronshtein that has raised $5M+. The comparable universe consists of 1 public company (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics.

Stage-progression valuation is the applicable methodology here, as peer-median triangulation cannot be reliably applied. The peer set lacks sufficient narrow-stage comparables (only 1 same-stage company identified across the robotics and manufacturing universe), making a filtered peer median uninformative. The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $5M total raised as a valuation proxy, implying a $12M valuation at the next stage milestone.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This range reflects single-method derivation and carries meaningful uncertainty. The primary limitation is sparse peer coverage within tight stage and valuation bands; a more robust triangulation would require either adjacent-stage comparables or a broader sector assessment. Key variables affecting outcomes include timing to Series A, capital efficiency, and market conditions at the next financing round.
